claims.text: A route deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The governing measurement under POL-RD-01 is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 26.44 km, against a booked optimal of 21.0 km — an excess of 5.44 km, which clears the 0.8 km absolute limb of the establishment test many times over.

The percentage limb of POL-RD-01 also passes: the excess is 25.90% of the 21.0 km optimal route, above the 20% threshold. Both limbs must pass and both do. I have deliberately cited the trace figure (26.44 km, EV-GPS-02801) rather than the rounded 26.4 km convenience copy on the trip record, because POL-RD-01 says the trace governs where the two disagree.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on the face of the bundle: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02801, and the trip record's start timestamp (2026-08-13T08:33:21) matches the first GPS fix on the trace (2026-08-13T08:33:21). These artifacts describe the same trip.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): it runs 208 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval (well under the 30 second ceiling), reports zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, and covers 100.0% of the trip. The independent-corroboration requirement of POL-RD-07(ii) is therefore not engaged, and neither is the mandatory escalation in POL-RD-10(3).

There is no rider-requested detour to excuse any part of the excess. The chat log for TRP-02801 contains 0 messages (message_count 0, first_message_at null, last_message_at null), and the trip record likewise records chat_message_count 0. With no rider instruction on file, the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 cannot be satisfied and the clause is unavailable; no distance is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

No pickup or dropoff relocation has occurred: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 therefore cannot be run on this record and supplies no adjusted baseline.

This was not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not apply: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and the matched-itinerary baseline that clause uses is not in play. The solo optimal of 21.0 km on the trip record is the correct baseline.

The fare was metered, not upfront-quoted, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd is null. POL-RD-02 is the clause that governs the refund on this trip.

The driver's only explanation — 'Traffic was heavy so I took another road', recorded in the counterparty statement — is an uncited traffic assertion. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory record naming a road the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, and there is none: EV-ADVIS-02801-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the comparison cannot be run and POL-RD-03 is unavailable. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. Under POL-RD-13 the missing advisory is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation either, because the driver names no evidence ID for an advisory and an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one; the assertion is discarded and the deviation stands at the measured figure. I disclose that the artifact I rely on for the absence carries weight 0.0.

The rider's own profile raises no corroboration hurdle: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so the additional-corroboration requirement that clause imposes on sub-30% claims does not apply here even if the excess were below 30%.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and comes out in the rider's favour. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 28.4) x 1.2 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 waiting time fee - 0 promo = 33.8024. Refund = 40.71 charged_total - 33.8024 = 6.9076, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 6.95.
The surge multiplier in that computation was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.2 — the only artifact on which the field appears — and not from any other source.

The refund of 6.9076 is far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so NO_ACTION under that head is unavailable, and at 16.97% of charged_total it is below the 90% full-refund share, so the remedy POL-RD-02 licenses is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 6.95, not a full one.

No pass-through correction arises under POL-RD-09 and none can be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure: the fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines, zero tolls and no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), so there is no off-route gantry and no phantom line to refund under POL-RD-09(4), and POL-RD-09(1) bars double-counting whatever the itemisation shows.

The deviation, though established, is not MATERIAL — 25.90% is below the 50% material_pct gate and 5.44 km is below the 8.0 km material_km gate — so I do not claim the POL-RD-06 uplift. For completeness, the driver's profile offers nothing that would aggravate the case in any event: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 191, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established.

NO_ACTION would be the wrong outcome here and would leave the rider carrying the whole charge: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the present state is that the rider has paid 40.71 including the 6.91 attributable to the unjustified detour. Under POL-GEN-03 a PARTIAL_REFUND returning that portion is what the evidence supports.

The deviation is established, but it is a small one: the GPS trace runs 26.44 km against the booked optimal of 21.0 km, an excess of 5.44 km or 25.9%. That clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate — more than 0.8 km and more than 20% — but it is well short of either materiality gate of 8.0 km or 50%, so this is an ordinary, non-MATERIAL deviation and must be treated as such.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation must carry the surge multiplier actually recorded on the fare breakdown — 1.2, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier — and must not treat surge as absent. On the optimal route the fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 28.4) x 1.2 + 0.80 = 33.8024, so the refund is 40.71 - 33.8024 = 6.9076, rounded up to SGD 6.95. Reading surge as absent would inflate the refund to roughly 12.41 and is wrong on this record.

The refund of 6.9076 is only 16.97% of the 40.71 charged, far below the 90%-of-charged_total share that converts a POL-RD-02 computation into a FULL_REFUND. The correct ruling value is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the POL-RD-02 quantum, and nothing larger.

Nothing may be added to the recomputed fare under POL-RD-09: the fare breakdown shows 0.00 of ERP and tolls, no Changi or Seletar airport surcharge, a 0.00 waiting-time fee and a 0.00 promo discount, and the trip neither originates nor terminates at an airport. There is no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity line to refund, so the driver's exposure does not increase beyond the distance-and-time figure.

Because the deviation is not MATERIAL, POL-RD-06 is not engaged at all: no driver_profile pattern test arises, the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral can be made on this trip. The remedy is confined to the POL-RD-02 recomputation against the booked optimal route.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, the driver_profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 191 — a ratio of 0.000, below the 0.05 test and short of the alternative 3-flag trigger. No pattern can be established on these two fields, which POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 make the only citable profile fields for this test; the lifetime counters on the same artifact are context only.

No exculpatory clause reduces the excess and POL-RD-02 therefore defines the whole of the driver's exposure: the chat log for this trip carries zero messages, so there is no POL-RD-04 rider instruction; the trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment and no amended optimal, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 is irrelevant; and the distance charged (26.4 km) matches the traced distance (26.44 km) to within 0.04 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall.

The driver's explanation was a traffic assertion, and the only advisory artifact for this trip is missing: EV-ADVIS-02801-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no advisory covering the Jurong Point corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and supplies no exoneration, as the driver accepts; equally, that missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an admission by the driver or a contradiction in the evidence, and the driver does not resist the measured excess on that ground.

Consistently, the driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d = 0 over completed_trips_90d = 191, so no repeat pattern is established.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. That clause applies because the fare model is METERED (fare_breakdown.fare_model, EV-FARE-02801) and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route. Surge is taken from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier = 1.2 — the only artifact carrying that field — and is not treated as absent. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 28.4) x 1.2 + 0.80 platform fee = (3.80 + 15.75 + 7.952) x 1.2 + 0.80 = 27.502 x 1.2 + 0.80 = 33.8024. Refund = charged_total 40.71 - 33.8024 = 6.9076, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 6.95. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 16.97% of charged_total, well below the 90% share that would convert this into a FULL_REFUND, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 6.95.

Nothing is added on top. The fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines, zero tolls, no airport surcharge and a 0.00 waiting-time fee, so POL-RD-09 yields no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity line; POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding off-route ERP to the POL-RD-02 figure in any event.
